title: Recording with Capitol singers and signing with Roulette
summary: Edison recorded with Nat Cole, Margaret Whiting, Bing Crosby, Ella and others, and stayed in Los Angeles because he was so busy.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Was that one -- how many pieces did you have?

Jimmy Forrest. It was the first date in Birdland, I signed a contract with Roulette, with Teddy Reig, you know, because he had been writing me. We had been corresponding. We're old friends, you know. And I didn't have a contract with anybody. My popularity was really flourishing at the time, you know. I was recording with all the singers. I did so many albums behind Nat Cole, Margaret Whiting.
Well, you were really in on that Capitol thing.
That was when Capitol was the hot label.
Hot label, right. And I recorded with Bing Crosby, Jerry Lewis, Billy Daniels, Ella Fitzgerald, oh, I recorded with everybody. I was really busy out here, you

know. That's the reason I stayed out here and didn't go back to New York, because I was doing the same thing out here as the guys were doing in New York. But, you know, they were going from one date to another, so was I, you know. And I was really, really busy out here.
Well, you were making good money then.
